paragraph: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether Burundi is making information or digital services accessible to persons with disabilities. No law, policy, programme, delivery or audit on digital accessibility has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying no law or policy addresses access to information or digital services for persons with disabilities.

In 2023-2024, [31 pupils trained at Sègbèya](<https://lanation.bj/numerique/inclusion-des-personnes-handicapees-au-benin-une-avancee-grace-aux-classes-numeriques>), one of three government digital classrooms for visually impaired learners in Benin. [Each has screen readers, braille printers and braille displays](<https://lanation.bj/numerique/inclusion-des-personnes-handicapees-au-benin-une-avancee-grace-aux-classes-numeriques>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule or programme for digital accessibility has been found, and no rule in force since October 2023 makes public information or digital services accessible. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[A project was launched on 8 August 2025 by Light for the World, UN-ABPAM and the Ministry of Secondary Education](<https://www.sidwaya.info/promotion-de-leducation-inclusive-un-projet-lance-pour-optimiser-lapprentissage-des-eleves-handicapes-visuels-par-le-numerique/>). [It aims to produce accessible digital lessons and exams](<https://www.sidwaya.info/promotion-de-leducation-inclusive-un-projet-lance-pour-optimiser-lapprentissage-des-eleves-handicapes-visuels-par-le-numerique/>). [It serves 48 visually impaired pupils and 34 teachers](<https://www.sidwaya.info/promotion-de-leducation-inclusive-un-projet-lance-pour-optimiser-lapprentissage-des-eleves-handicapes-visuels-par-le-numerique/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force, and no audit of public websites or digital services has been found. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether Botswana is making information or digital services accessible to persons with disabilities. No law, policy, programme, delivery or audit on digital accessibility has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying no law or policy addresses access to information or digital services for persons with disabilities.

[On 26 June 2025 the employment ministry received a job site for job-seekers with disabilities](<https://www.emploi.gouv.ci/uploads/publications/17509697364.pdf>). [It also received multimedia rooms at the School for the Deaf and a university, and a pupils' YouTube channel](<https://www.emploi.gouv.ci/uploads/publications/17509697364.pdf>). The MTN Foundation built them under a convention with the ministry. [CIPESA says the Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalization is reviewing its digital transition policy](<https://cipesa.org/2025/11/100-activists-trained-to-advance-digital-inclusion-for-persons-with-disabilities-in-cote-divoire/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives the results of an accessibility audit of public websites or digital services. Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

[In February 2024 PATNUC, at MINPOSTEL, sought a consultant to update the 2020 digital plan](<https://armp.cm/details?id_publication=787&type_publication=DP>). [The update adds accessibility and gender equality](<https://armp.cm/details?id_publication=787&type_publication=DP>). [In June 2025 a CIPESA legal analysis found no national law or policy on ICT access for persons with disabilities](<https://cipesa.org/wp-content/files/Legal_Analysis_of_Technology_and_DisabilityinAfrica.pdf>), and only general disability laws apply. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[In 2020 G3ict's DARE Index recorded DRC policies on accessible web, TV, mobile telephony and digital content](<https://g3ict.org/country-profile/congo-democratic-republic-of>). [It rated each at implementation level 5 of 5](<https://g3ict.org/country-profile/congo-democratic-republic-of>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026, [the WSIS Forum 2026 session description says HandiConnect lets users access state services and G2P social-protection payments on basic feature phones via USSD](<https://www.itu.int/net4/wsis/forum/2026/Agenda/Session/220>). [The DRC Ministry of Telecommunications, the Ministry delegated to Persons with Disabilities and FONA back it](<https://www.itu.int/net4/wsis/forum/2026/Agenda/Session/220>). No source found since October 2023 gives the results of an accessibility audit. Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

[In January 2026 a civil-society submission said Comoros's 2014 disability law, no. 14-037/AU, does not take up accessibility (CRPD article 9)](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/JS3_UPR46_COM_F_Main.pdf>). [Nor does it take up reasonable accommodation](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/JS3_UPR46_COM_F_Main.pdf>). [The law also lacks provisions on freedom of expression and access to information](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/JS3_UPR46_COM_F_Main.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says digital accessibility is under way. Preparing would need a government body to draft, launch or prepare a law, policy, standard or programme on accessible information or digital services.

[The labour inspectorate's portal, launched on 3 November 2026, has text-to-speech and keyboard navigation](<https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/ilo-supports-digital-transformation-cabo-verde%E2%80%99s-general-labour>). [It also works with screen readers and has better colour contrast, the ILO reports](<https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/ilo-supports-digital-transformation-cabo-verde%E2%80%99s-general-labour>). The portal was launched in the last twelve months, and no earlier accessibility position has been found for Cape Verde. No law, policy, standard or programme on digital accessibility for persons with disabilities has been found. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

In July 2024 the National Agency for Persons with Disabilities (ANPH) [held a workshop on its survey of sign language use](<https://www.lanation.dj/anph-mieux-comprendre-lusage-et-la-connaissance-des-langues-des-signes-parmi-les-personnes-malentendantes/>). The survey is to digitise the Djiboutian sign language dictionary. In October 2024 [an ANPH concept note presented a hackathon to build Mobile ID apps](<https://evenement.anph.dj/pdf/note.pdf>) for access to public services. [Law 151/AN/22 of July 2022](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/113314/DJI-113314.pdf>) asks the State to ensure access to information and electronic services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule in force since October 2023 has been found. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[Executive decree 26-98 of 31 January 2026 requires ministries to make information accessible to persons with specific needs](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2026/F2026013.pdf>). [It names braille, adapted computing, sign language and subtitling](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2026/F2026013.pdf>). [It also requires adapted ICT equipment for pupils, students and trainees](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2026/F2026013.pdf>). The decree dates from the last twelve months. [The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications ran app contests for people with specific needs in 2021 and 2022](<https://www.mpt.gov.dz/coordination-qualitative-avec-differents-secteurs/autonomisation-des-personnes-a-besoins-specifiques/>). No source found since October 2023 says accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered. Operating would need a government body to deliver accessible digital services or assistive technology, or to make public websites or broadcasts accessible.

In September 2026 [the Ministry of Transport added accessibility tools to its website, including text-to-speech and a sign-language interpreter](<https://www.youm7.com/story/2026/9/17/%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AA%D8%B7%D9%84%D9%82-%D8%AE%D8%AF%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D8%AA%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%B0%D9%88%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%87%D9%85%D9%85-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%88%D9%82%D8%B9%D9%87%D8%A7/7549148>). In the last twelve months, [in November 2026 the social solidarity and ICT ministries signed a protocol with the Public Prosecution, Orange and e-finance](<https://arqam.news/610073/>). It is to ease disabled people's electronic access to prosecution services. [NTRA and the Central Bank required mobile operators to make e-wallets accessible](<https://www.tra.gov.eg/en/ntra-issues-instructions-to-facilitate-the-use-of-mobile-e-wallet-services-for-people-of-determination/>). No source found since October 2023 gives the results of an accessibility audit. Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

No stage is set. In October 2025 WMO reported that [Ethiopia's early warnings reach persons with disabilities in accessible formats](<https://wmo.int/media/update/from-global-commitment-local-action-early-warnings-all-shows-real-progress>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since October 2023 says a government body drafted or adopted a law, policy or programme on accessible information or digital services. Preparing would need a government body to draft, launch or prepare a law, policy, standard or programme on accessible information or digital services.

[The Bank of Ghana's January 2025 directive requires financial providers to make websites and digital channels disability friendly](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Financial-Inclusion-for-Persons-with-Disabilities-Directive.pdf>). [It names voice and audio controls, larger font and sign-language videos](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Financial-Inclusion-for-Persons-with-Disabilities-Directive.pdf>). [It sets administrative penalties for providers that do not comply](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Financial-Inclusion-for-Persons-with-Disabilities-Directive.pdf>). [Ghana says the National Communication Authority has taken measures to make GTV news broadcasts accessible to the deaf](<https://docstore.ohchr.org/SelfServices/FilesHandler.ashx?enc=u%2F7HeWsLeAGf4bOeOKu3awum%2BSewPd75x9YtJIsnfd7wWVeIkx7T8atLYZizIHJzk1touKDXHXm66ALasS%2BmMw%3D%3D>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

In June 2025 the Ministry of Planning [launched the Lonnin Fanka programme](<https://africa-news-agency.com/guinea-launch-of-lonnin-fanka-to-bridge-digital-divide-and-train-youth/>). It aims to give every Guinean, people with disabilities among them, a computer, internet access and certified training. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the ECOWAS Commission [met Guinean authorities and disability groups in Conakry](<https://www.guinee7.com/2026/06/25/inclusion-la-cedeao-renforce-son-engagement-en-faveur-des-enfants-en-situation-de-handicap-en-guinee/>) to discuss the third phase of its assistive-devices programme for children. It covers specialised tablets among other devices, with USD 300,000 committed. No source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[In April 2026 PURA issued draft Broadcasting and Online Content Regulations, 2026, for consultation](<https://pura.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Broadcasting-and-Online-Content-Regulations-2026-.pdf>). [Their arrangement lists regulation 62, on content for persons with disabilities](<https://pura.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Broadcasting-and-Online-Content-Regulations-2026-.pdf>). [Regulation 63 covers mandatory sign language and aids](<https://pura.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Broadcasting-and-Online-Content-Regulations-2026-.pdf>). The draft dates from the last twelve months, and no source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[The Universal Service Fund's portfolio includes an assistive technology project](<https://www.kictanet.or.ke/major-usf-transparency-update-kenyas-communications-authority-responds-to-public-inquiry/>), giving content and devices to learners with print disabilities, as listed in August 2025. In the last twelve months, [on 30 October 2026 officials validated a roadmap for digital and ICT accessibility](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-10-31-state-plans-digital-accessibility-audits-to-improve-services-for-pwds>). Public institutions are to audit their websites and online platforms. [On 12 August 2026 the National Assembly passed the Public Participation Bill](<https://nation.africa/kenya/news/mps-pass-public-participation-law-here-is-what-it-means-for-you-5558002>), which requires authorities to make participation accessible to persons with disabilities. It awaited presidential assent. No rule in force found since October 2023 makes public information or digital services accessible. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[In May 2026 the National Commission on Disabilities launched its 2026-2030 Five-Year Strategic Plan](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/ncd-launches-five-year-strategic-plan-and-2026-psip-project/>). [The plan proposes a Sign Language and Braille Education department](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/ncd-launches-five-year-strategic-plan-and-2026-psip-project/>). It is the nearest fact found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force, or that accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

A September 2026 paper says [Libya issued its National Digital Accessibility Policy in December 2024](<https://journal.utripoli.edu.ly/index.php/Alqalam/article/download/1972/1479/4024>). It describes the policy as mandatory, based on WCAG 2.2, with a timetable from 2025 to 2030. The General Information Authority dates [its adoption to April 2025](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/02/04/the-general-authority-for-information-launches-the-actual-implementation-path-of-the-national-digital-accessibility-policy-in-collaboration-with-escwa/>). On 28 January 2026 the Authority and ESCWA [began putting the policy into effect](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/02/04/the-general-authority-for-information-launches-the-actual-implementation-path-of-the-national-digital-accessibility-policy-in-collaboration-with-escwa/>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, two ministers [launched the Wasl initiative](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=367274&lang=ar>), one of whose tracks eases access of persons with disabilities to services. No delivery of accessible services by a government body has been found. The September 2026 audit is an academic paper. Operating would need a government body to deliver accessible digital services or assistive technology, or to make public websites or broadcasts accessible.

[The ICT ministry and Vodacom opened a digital library for persons with disabilities at the State Library in Maseru](<https://www.gov.ls/education/4g-enabled-digital-library-unveiled-for-persons-with-disability-in-maseru/>) in March 2026. [It has a Braille printer and eye-tracking technology](<https://www.gov.ls/education/4g-enabled-digital-library-unveiled-for-persons-with-disability-in-maseru/>). The centre opened in the last twelve months, and no earlier accessibility position has been found for Lesotho. No rule or programme for digital accessibility has been found. No rule in force found since October 2023 makes public information or digital services accessible. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

A joint study by the Mediator, the National Observatory of Human Development and the Secretariat of State for Social Inclusion [was presented in March 2026](<https://fr.le360.ma/societe/personnes-en-situation-de-handicap-seules-25-des-administrations-marocaines-sont-inclusives-le_IH7JZFEDLJHUTK5V2MM3YSNIFY/>). It found 47.5% of public institutions offer inclusive digital solutions. It rated 25% of administrations inclusive overall. In June 2026 the broadcasting regulator HACA issued [decision 50-26 on the 2026 elections](<https://www.haca.ma/sites/default/files/upload/CSCA_D%C3%A9cision%20n%C2%B050-26_Elections%202026%20VF.pdf>), which requires audiovisual services to give persons with disabilities access to election programmes. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the digital transition ministry [launched a new version of the Idarati portal](<https://www.mmsp.gov.ma/fr/actualites/idarati-vers-une-administration-plus-proche-proactive-et-centr%C3%A9e-sur-le-citoyen>), redesigned for digital accessibility. That month the minister [held a consultation on digital public services for persons with disabilities](<https://lenew.ma/inclusion-numerique-le-gouvernement-mise-sur-les-jeunes-les-femmes-et-les-personnes-en-situation-de-handicap/>).

[On 3 December 2025 the Prime Minister sent Parliament draft law 017/2025 on access to public information](<https://pub-7e0d3a35c1b949698a7ced344fa56252.r2.dev/textes/017-2025/PROJET_LAICP___PR_SENT_E_AU.PDF>). [It says public information must be adapted for persons with disabilities](<https://pub-7e0d3a35c1b949698a7ced344fa56252.r2.dev/textes/017-2025/PROJET_LAICP___PR_SENT_E_AU.PDF>). [It names specialised media, adapted technologies and human assistance](<https://pub-7e0d3a35c1b949698a7ced344fa56252.r2.dev/textes/017-2025/PROJET_LAICP___PR_SENT_E_AU.PDF>). The draft was sent in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a rule is in force. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[Lei 10/2024 of 7 June 2024 gives persons with disabilities a right of access to information technologies](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz228091.pdf>). [It says public services should give information in accessible formats](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz228091.pdf>). [It also asks for sign-language training for State communicators](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz228091.pdf>). [The ITU-EU VaMoz Digital project supports the government from 2023 to 2027](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Regional-Presence/Africa/Pages/projects/2023/mozambique-vamoz-digital.aspx>). [It trained more than 320 stakeholders, according to ITU](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Regional-Presence/Africa/Pages/projects/2023/mozambique-vamoz-digital.aspx>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered. Operating would need a government body to deliver accessible digital services or assistive technology, or to make public websites or broadcasts accessible.

In August 2026 the ICT ministry released its [Digital Service Framework](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Digital-Service-Framework.pdf>). It says ministries must adhere to it and requires all digital services to comply with WCAG 2.1 Level AA. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, [the AI Unit's website offered built-in accessibility tools](<https://aim.govmu.org/aim/accessibility>), and the unit says [it fixed all critical issues found in a May 2026 audit of its website](<https://aim.govmu.org/aim/accessibility>). It publishes no other findings. In September 2025 [a Mauritian Sign Language e-dictionary was launched at the Beau-Bassin school for the deaf](<https://www.lemauricien.com/actualites/societe/ecole-des-sourds-lancement-dun-dictionnaire-electronique-de-langue-des-signes/683699/>). Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

[Section 30 of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2024 has been in force since April 2024](<https://macoda.mw/public/assets/uploads/publications/240812090242_Persons%20with%20Disabilities%20Act,%202024.pdf>). [It requires anyone publishing information to the public to publish it in accessible formats](<https://macoda.mw/public/assets/uploads/publications/240812090242_Persons%20with%20Disabilities%20Act,%202024.pdf>). [It names sign language and braille](<https://macoda.mw/public/assets/uploads/publications/240812090242_Persons%20with%20Disabilities%20Act,%202024.pdf>). [The National Disability Policy 2025 commits the government to information in accessible formats](<https://macoda.mw/public/assets/uploads/publications/250812084349_NATIONAL%20DISABILITY%20POLICY.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered. Operating would need a government body to deliver accessible digital services or assistive technology, or to make public websites or broadcasts accessible.

[Paradigm Initiative's 2023 report finds nothing on digital inclusion of persons with disabilities beyond a vague broadband-policy reference](<https://paradigmhq.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Namibia-Country-Report.pdf>). [It says the 2004 Disability Act does not mention the internet](<https://paradigmhq.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Namibia-Country-Report.pdf>). [In 2021 researchers tested selected government websites with Lighthouse, WAVE, the W3C validator, ChromeVox and an alt-text tester](<https://www.springerprofessional.de/an-investigation-of-e-government-web-accessibility-for-visually-/19702690>). [The automatic tools gave varied and inconclusive results](<https://www.springerprofessional.de/an-investigation-of-e-government-web-accessibility-for-visually-/19702690>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says digital accessibility is under way. Preparing would need a government body to draft, launch or prepare a law, policy, standard or programme on accessible information or digital services.

A TechCabal article of August 2026 says [NITDA's Standards and Guidelines for Government Websites require government institutions to adopt WCAG](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/31/nigeria-wants-assistive-tech-who-is-fixing-its-inaccessible-digital-platforms/>). [An assessment presented to NITDA by researcher Tracy Onabis Agbamu found only 47% of about 30 government digital platforms met the accessibility threshold](<https://www.itweb.africa/article/nigerian-govt-platforms-fail-access-test/KA3Ww7dzPjkqrydZ>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026, [NITDA said it is looking to advance national accessibility standards](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/16/nitda-strengthens-digital-accessibility-persons-with-disabilities/>). In October 2026 GovInsider reported that an Open Government Partnership group [working with NITDA plans to pilot standards](<https://govinsider.asia/intl-en/article/the-jargon-problem-keeping-public-participation-out-of-dpi-design-1>). The pilot covers 10 federal agencies within two years.

In 2025 RISA's Government of Rwanda Websites Guideline said [all government websites must meet or exceed WCAG 2.2](<https://guidelines.risa.gov.rw/books/government-of-rwanda-websites-guideline/page/accessibility>). GPE reports that [the Rwanda Basic Education Board had recorded 96 edutainment episodes by September 2024](<https://www.globalpartnership.org/results/country-journeys/rwanda-education-goes-digital>). They carry sign language for deaf children and audio for blind children. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No published audit of public websites or digital services has been found since October 2023. Mature would need the published results of an audit or survey of how accessible public websites or digital services are.

No stage is set. [Sudan's Persons with Disability National Act 2017](<https://www.apminebanconvention.org/fileadmin/_APMBC-DOCUMENTS/StatePlans-policies/Sudan_Disability_Law_Translated_2017.pdf>) provides for sign language with on-screen text in media programmes, and for access to electronic services. In December 2017 the telecoms regulator [opened the first phase of its Ibsar project](<https://tpra3.onespace.sd/en/projects/ibsar-project/>), training visually impaired people in computer and internet use. In the last twelve months, [a study published in April 2026 tested seven Sudanese academic, government and service websites against WCAG 2.1 AA](<https://doi.org/10.56961/mejeit.v5i1.1442>) and found critical barriers on every site. It is an academic study. No rule in force, programme or delivery since October 2023 has been found. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.

[In September 2026 the president of ISOC Senegal said there is not yet a clear policy to include persons with disabilities](<https://lesoleil.sn/actualites/societe-fait-divers/inclusion-des-personnes-handicapees-cheikh-ahmadou-bamba-mbacke-de-lopen-society-senegal-appelle-a-un-cadre-juridique-pour-laccessibilite-numerique/>). [The same speaker called for guidelines and a law on digital accessibility](<https://lesoleil.sn/actualites/societe-fait-divers/inclusion-des-personnes-handicapees-cheikh-ahmadou-bamba-mbacke-de-lopen-society-senegal-appelle-a-un-cadre-juridique-pour-laccessibilite-numerique/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says digital accessibility is under way, and no delivery or audit has been found. Preparing would need a government body to draft, launch or prepare a law, policy, standard or programme on accessible information or digital services.

[In 2025 MoCTI handed assistive devices to four disability institutions in Makeni, Kenema and Freetown](<https://sldtp.gov.sl/2025/11/12/mocti-hands-over-assistive-devices-to-disability-institutions-with-support-from-sldtp/>). [They include screen-reader computers, Braille note takers and embossers](<https://sldtp.gov.sl/2025/11/12/mocti-hands-over-assistive-devices-to-disability-institutions-with-support-from-sldtp/>). In the last twelve months, [on 22 October 2026 two government bodies validated Leh Wi Tok, a communication app for speech- and hearing-impaired people](<https://www.sierraleonepress.com/dsti-and-social-welfare-validate-new-app-for-speech-and-hearing-impaired-in-sierra-leone/>). [The Social Welfare minister plans to take it to cabinet](<https://www.sierraleonepress.com/dsti-and-social-welfare-validate-new-app-for-speech-and-hearing-impaired-in-sierra-leone/>). No law or standard in force requiring accessible public websites has been found. Establishing would need a law, regulation, policy or standard in force that requires accessible public information, websites or digital services.
